kicker: Done learning from others' gardens — now plant your own.
summary: AI is a shared garden — how you tend it is your own.

quiz.q: You're just starting, on an ordinary laptop, and don't want to spend money yet. What's the most sensible first step?
options: Buy a powerful computer to run AI locally
Use a chat assistant's free plan and practise clear briefs and fact-checking
Sign up for lots of platforms at once
Wait until AI is perfect before learning
quiz.explain: Clear briefs and verification are the base skills and work with every tool. Add tools once you know what you need.

ask.label: Four questions by the pond
ask.art: Looking almost straight down at a pond at first light: four stepping stones run diagonally across it to a stone lantern on the far bank, pebbles and the shadows of two koi on the bottom. Each stone is engraved with a question; the answers float round it like lotus leaves. Choose a leaf and it drifts to the stone, ripples spread and the next stone rises out of the water. After all four, the view pulls back over the whole path and the far lantern lights up.
ask.privacy: Your answers stay in your browser and are never sent anywhere.

questions.q: What do you most want AI to help with?

options.label: Understand it to manage and decide
A powerful machine: lots of RAM, a graphics card

insight.text: A good toolkit starts from your work, not from a list of trending tools.

kit.label: Your suggested toolkit
kit.art: A close view of a lidded rattan basket on a wooden veranda table, the first ray of sun coming low from the right, the basket throwing a long shadow to the left. Lift the lid and the tools that fit your answers by the pond float up inside: a brush, a colour box with an ink stick and a vermilion cake, a small oil lamp, a wood plane, a scroll tied with cord. Whatever doesn’t fit lies outside on the table, faint as a moon shadow. Touch a tool and it floats toward you as its paper card opens.
kit.empty: Answer the four questions by the pond and the basket will pack itself.

types.name: Chat assistant
types.what: Ask, write, summarise, brainstorm. The base of every toolkit.

types.name: Image & video tools
types.what: Create, edit and upscale images; make short videos. Usually paid in credits.

types.name: AI on your own machine
types.what: Download an open model and run it on your computer: private, works offline. Needs enough RAM.

types.name: Coding agent
types.what: You describe it in words; the agent writes, runs and fixes the code. Good for mini apps and games.

types.name: Skills & workflows
types.what: Package repeated work as reusable instructions (SKILL.md), then chain them into a workflow.

phone.note: On a phone: use the chat assistant app and the web or app versions of image and video tools.

laptop.note: An ordinary laptop can run small models; try local AI when you need to keep data private.

strong.note: Powerful machine: try running open models locally, so your data never leaves it.

free.note: Most tools have a limited free plan. Starting with one chat assistant is enough.

mid.note: Pay for the one tool you use most; avoid piling up subscriptions.

invest.note: Invest in tools for your main work and in time to learn; track your credits every month.

priceNote.text: Prices and features change often; always check the official page before you pay.

insight.text: Choose by type of work first, tool name second: tools change monthly, your work changes less.

path.label: A 30-day path
path.art: From the veranda step, looking up a backlit moss slope: a gravel path leads to a garden gate on the horizon, the sun about to rise behind it, a thin moon still in the corner of the sky. Four empty hollows wait along the path, each farther one smaller; four week-stones lie on the veranda floor. Lay them in order and the sun clears the gate while a ray runs down the path, waking each stone.
path.keys: Press 1 to 4 to lay the stones in order
path.wrong: This stone needs the previous week as its base.
path.done: The path is lit. Each week has a take-away card.

steps.label: Week 1 · Disciplined chat
steps.detail: Every day, give a chat assistant one real task: state the role, context and output; always verify one detail.
steps.why: Clear briefs and verification are the base for every other tool.

steps.label: Week 2 · One finished asset
steps.detail: Finish one piece: an image, a short video or a post. From brief to many drafts, choosing, editing, then checking rights and labelling it as AI-made.
steps.why: Only a full loop shows where AI helps and where your hands are needed.

steps.label: Week 3 · Turn a repeated task into a skill
steps.detail: Pick something you do every week, write down the steps from a time it went well, have AI turn them into a SKILL.md, and test it three times.
steps.why: From then on AI remembers how you work, so you don't have to repeat yourself every day.

steps.label: Week 4 · Build a mini app yourself
steps.detail: Write a one-page spec for a small app or game, have a coding agent build it piece by piece, test it, fix each bug.
steps.why: You reuse everything you've learned: describe clearly, break it down, verify, save it.

insight.text: One stone a week, each resting on the last: discipline, a product, a habit, then building your own tool.

advice.label: Learning that lasts
advice.art: The camera lies in the moss: a rain puddle mirrors the dawn, with three stone lanterns around it — a huge one close on the left, one on the right, one far beyond the water. Each lays a wedge of light on the water. A red maple leaf floats in the middle with three soft shadows spreading three ways. Steer the leaf toward a lantern and it brightens, its shadow shortens and its words appear.
advice.group: Three views on learning with AI

view.text: Bring AI into every part of your work to see for yourself where it shines and where it fails; respect rules, ethics and privacy.
The more people trusted AI, the less they thought critically; those confident in their own expertise questioned more. This is a correlation, self-reported.

stones.who: MIT Media Lab · experiment with 54 people, 2025

view.text: The group writing essays with ChatGPT showed the weakest brain connectivity (measured by EEG), compared with search-engine users and those writing unaided. A small study, not yet peer-reviewed.

common.text: Use AI a lot to learn fast, but keep the thinking and checking for yourself.

insight.text: AI is a good companion while you keep the wheel: think first, ask AI second, then check.

enso.label: Your ensō
enso.art: Dawn over a raked sand garden, seen from just above the sand. Draw an ensō in one stroke: the sun flares and the camera cranes up over the garden, where every Moon Garden station you visited rises as a stone inside the circle and every station not yet visited waits as a raked hollow. At the ring’s open mouth lie a vermilion seal on a sheet of paper and a furoshiki cloth bundle.
enso.drawAria: Draw the ensō that sums up your journey
enso.toolkitAria: Open the Toolkit: every Part 2 take-away card

insight.text: The moonlit journey ends here. The next garden is the one you plant yourself, a little each day.
